Career profile · Harvard International Office

Narissara Khomkhai

Associate Director, Operations & Administration

I build the operating system behind international education: clean records, reliable systems, reporting leaders can defend, and a team that can absorb peak work. My experience spans higher-education operations, data and systems — advancement services at Phillips Academy and UAMS, then governed reporting and cross-unit coordination at Harvard FAS.

Career profile · Harvard International Office · Cambridge, Massachusetts. The work sample is linked here; this page is the experience behind it.

Why HIO

HIO’s work is a chain: a School record becomes a SEVIS record, a federal deadline becomes an advisor’s day, a service becomes a bill, and a report becomes a decision. I have spent my career making that kind of chain accurate, testable and easier to run. The work sample is my proposed operating model; this profile is the experience behind it.

Record-to-form process map

Proposed control sequence

  1. ReceiveSchool file or Slate export; source date and owner
  2. CrosswalkSchool program code to SEVIS code
  3. ValidateName, birth date, dates, funding and program
  4. DraftAdvisor drafts the I-20 or DS-2019
  5. BatchOperations submits and reviews every SEVIS response
  6. ReviewException closed by a person, with a date and owner

Control: no form is issued from an unvalidated record. The record, the reason and the owner stay together.

03 HIO fit

What transfers to HIO — and what I would learn on the job

I have not served as a DSO or ARO. I am a U.S. citizen and eligible for designation. The transferable core is record integrity, system ownership, reporting discipline, billing controls, team leadership and data security; SEVIS practice would be learned through formal training, shadowing and supervised signing before independent case decisions.

01

Record integrity

Audit-ready gift and faculty records; duplicate prevention; exception logs; reconciliation before release.

HIO application Five checks before a form; every mismatch goes to a person.

02

Systems and conversions

Three platform conversions: requirements, mapping, parallel run, rollback, training and vendor management.

HIO application ISSM modernization, release gates and HUIT architecture review.

03

Reporting and data

DataHub across seven sources; SQL and BI; one definition per measure; legal and compliance request handling.

HIO application The Director’s dashboard and a single source for recurring numbers.

04

Billing and reconciliation

$400M campaign-to-General-Ledger reconciliation; 20K+ annual transactions; online payments; dispute and accrual work.

HIO application Hospital invoices, service log, aging and credit decisions.

05

Team and office operations

Eight years supervising 3–5 staff; hiring, reviews, cross-training and peak planning.

HIO application One queue, WIP limits, named backups and a calm peak.

06

Security and audit

Role- and hierarchy-based access; confidential records; documented controls; vendor oversight.

HIO application Least privilege, quarterly access review and incident readiness.
